title: Judge OCEAN scores and Bridge replies with Jev
body: ## Summary Jev now judges two places Gemini used to grade itself. - After a Mirror interview, one decision call checks each OCEAN score against the user's own answers. A mismatch can be accepted as a move into the neighboring band (below 30, 30–70, or above 70). Preset profiles skip this check. - After a Bridge comparison, a second call reports whether the aligned reply applies the steering directives, whether the unaligned reply applies the inverse, whether the two replies actually differ, and whether each highlight explains the mechanism or only restates the advice. A column under the 0.7 gate is labeled weak alignment. - The psychometric eval uses the same question spec and branches on `choice` and `noul`. It no longer searches Gemini prose for `EVALUATION: FAIL` or `VERIFICATION: FAIL`. Without `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, the eval records `judge skipped` and the UI hides the check so the preset demo still works. The key stays on the `judgeProxy` Cloud Function. The browser calls `/api/judge`. ## Walkthrough ## Test plan - [x] `npm run test` (56 passed; Firestore teardown still prints the known unauthenticated delete error) - [x] `python3 scripts/test_jev_judge.py` and `python3 scripts/agent_eval.py --validate-matrix` - [x] Preset profile proceeds to The Tailor with no independent check - [x] A judged interview offers `85 → 50` for a too-high Conscientiousness score and The Tailor receives 50 - [x] The Bridge labels the unaligned column weak alignment and shows 41% in Logic Analysis
